card: Backports Guix build configuration fixes from master to the 32.x maintenance branch to re-enable building release binaries on RISC-V hardware. It updates the Guix time-machine commit, skips failing tests for packages on riscv64, and addresses Python 3.12 incompatibilities with setuptools and certvalidator. This backports upstream fixes from PR #36233 and PR #36425, resolving issue #36232 for the 32.x release cycle.
evidence: Commit a5e6a09956 notes it 'is necessary to unblock building on RISC-V systems' and fixes issue #36232.
Commit 58938225a1 explains that python-lief and nsis-x86_64 transitively pull in packages whose tests fail when building natively on riscv64.
PR description states: 'These backports re-enable building release binaries on RISC-V hardware.'
problem: Deterministic release binaries cannot be built natively on RISC-V hardware on the 32.x branch due to package test failures and Guix time-machine limitations. In addition, updating to Python 3.12 broke Guix builds requiring setuptools and the test loader in certvalidator.

risk.why: Mistakes in Guix manifests or time-machine revisions affect release binary reproducibility and builder toolchains.

scope_notes: The 4 commits in the PR only touch 4 Guix files (+42/-11), but the diff provided against the merge base includes numerous unrelated branch commits from 32.x vs master.
summary: Backports Guix build configuration updates from master to the 32.x maintenance branch. It bumps the Guix time-machine commit, skips tests that fail during native builds on riscv64, explicitly declares python-setuptools, and updates certvalidator for Python 3.12 compatibility.
